newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - July 3.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
DAILY TELEGRAPH-- POWER CHIEFS SHARE 2.6 MILLION STG BONANZA

The annual report and accounts of power company National Power have revealed that executive directors have shared profits of more than 2.6 million stg over the last two years from exercising share options. According to the accounts, performance bonuses for executive directors averaged 28 per cent to 32 per cent of basic salary. The pay package of Keith Harvey, the group's chief executive, rose by 40 per cent to more than 628,000 pounds stg in the year to March 31. -- BRITISH GAS TAKES 37 MILLION STG INDIAN STAKE

British Gas GAS.L is to pay 25.7 million stg to take a 44.3 per cent stake in Gujarata Gas, India's biggest gas distribution company. BG will also launch a public tender - in compliance with Indian takeover regulations - worth 11.6 million stg for an additional 20 per cent of the equity. The move will give BG control of the Indian company, which supplies customers in the western state of Gujarat. -- FYFFES HUNGRY FOR TARGETS AS SALES SLIP

Fyffes, the fresh fruit and vegetable group, has reported a 2.6 per cent fall in half-year pre-tax profits, to 20.2 million stg. The results were in line with a warning issued by the group in April that unfavourable currency trends and a drop in supermarket prices for its goods would affect results this year. Announcing the results, chairman Neil McCann said the group was 'actively looking' for substantial acquisitions.
THE TIMES -- BT CALLS TRUCE AFTER WINDFALL ESCAPE

British Telecom will no longer challenge the government over its windfall tax fines after discovering that the new tax would only cost it 500m stg. BT chairman Sir Iain Vallance declared that his company remains opposed to the levy on whole, as it represents a tax on 'success, not on excess'. Analysts had predicted the tax on BT could have been as high as one billion dollars. -- KALAMAZOO FINDS 1.2 MILLION STG BLACK HOLE

Computer services and printing group Kalamazoo has discovered a 1.2 million stg 'black hole' in the books of its accounting software division. The company blamed the loss on unnamed managers, since dismissed, who covered up disappointing trading results by keying-in phantom profits. The discovery comes as Kalamazoo is in talks with potential bidders. -- CONSUMERS' ASSOCIATION DEFENDS 'BEST VISA' CLAIM

The Consumers' Association has approved the decision by Which? magazine to recommend its own credit card as a 'best buy' in August issue which features a survey on best credit cards for those who spend 2,700 per year and pay for three or four bills in full. CA product development manager Chris Peers said the card is aimed at Which? members who pay off their card in full at the end of each month and not those who 'only pay the minimum' and added that Which? Visa members 'are mostly middle aged and affluent'.
THE GUARDIAN -- PEACE MOVES IN MOET MERGER

Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods company LVMH, met with the chairmen of Guinness and Grand Metropolitan on Wednesday for talks on how to progress on the proposed merger between the two drinks giants. LVMH is opposed to the 24 billion stg deal, but it is understood that Arnault was asked to come up with written proposals on how to 'create shareholder value', including suggestions on how best to inject LVMH's spirits operation into the proposed deal. -- ITALIANS JOIN THE TELECOM PARTY WITH AT&T DEAL

Stet, the Italian national telecoms company, has unveiled an anticipated global strategic alliance with America's AT&T and the Unisource consortium. The US firm is expected to take a 5 per cent stake in Stet, which is due to be privatised in October. The move will allow Stet - as part of the consortium - to target multinational companies in Europe and Latin America and to compete with rival international telecoms alliances. -- CLINTON SEEKS INTERNET FREE-TRADE ZONE

US President Bill Clinton has signalled his determination to turn the Internet into a 'free-trade zone'. In a move which will boost the prospects for electronic commerce, Clinton pledged late Tuesday to have policies on privacy, patents and copyright in place within a year, and he outlined a 13-point plan to achieve this objective. However, Clinton's vision could run into trouble with US state officials and European authorities who see Internet trading as a new source of tax revenue.
THE INDEPENDENT -- SUN LIFE TO BUY AXA FOR 690 MILLION STG

Sun Life and Provincial is to buy rival life insurer Axa Equity & Law in a complex 690 million stg deal. Both companies are owned by the giant French insurance company Axa-UAP, which will retain majority-ownership of the new, enlarged Sun Life organisation. The new Sun Life group, which will be the third- largest life insurer in the UK, will have 30 billion stg in funds under management and a stock market value of 2.5 billion stg. -- SBC WARBURG TOPS INVESTMENT ANALYSTS SURVEY

The 1997 Extel Survey of Investment Analysts has placed SBC Warburg at the top of the All Sectors League. The ranking comes as another blow to the investment banking arm of NatWest, last years winner, which was placed second this year. NatWest Securities recently lost its chief executive Martin Owen. Third place in the rankings went to Merrill Lynch, up from sixth last year. -- SEARS IN GREAT SHOPS GIVEAWAY

Retail group Sears is to give away chargecards and up to 6,000 pounds stg in spending money to estate agents who buy unwanted shops from the group on behalf of their clients. Sears has introduced the 'Play Lucky Lettings' promotion as it struggles to offload some 135 properties. The 'marketing' scheme also includes cash payments and up to six months free rent on some locations.
